about: WP-4 first-use trial seed. Deliberately non-sensitive Sovereign project knowledge, all of it already public in this repository. Each record is a short governed note whose `source` points back to its authoritative Git location; it does not copy the ADRs. Git stays authoritative: if a note disagrees with Git, Git wins and the note should be corrected or contested. Claims arrive as unverified proposals for the founder to review.

records.content: Why the first second-brain graph is computed on read: its provenance edges (claim supported by record, record corrects record, claim supersedes claim) are links the vault already stores, so a graph computed on read adds no new authority, no new table and no Forget burden, and never changes what a model may see (ADR-0005 section 8.1, retrieval position R3).

Issue #6 is what blocks SB-2 from ever holding real data: raw SQLite REPLACE statements naming a hidden rowid bypass the storage triggers, and an approved claim stripped of all evidence links still counted as supported. A repair (schema 5, rowid-free canonical tables) is proposed in PR #10 and awaits independent audit and founder approval.
SB-2 is blocked until the Issue #6 storage repair is merged.

Correction: SB-2 development is not blocked. SB-2a needs no schema change and can be built and audited on synthetic data; the Issue #6 repair is required before any real personal data, not before development.

What changed after the independent architecture audit of 2026-10-22: the authority kernel was narrowed to K1 canonical store, K2 governed context and disclosure, and K3 action gate (represented, not built); SB-2 was split into SB-2a navigation and SB-2b exporter; Builder 0 practices started immediately; capture became its own lane separated from permission to store sensitive data.
The same audit found that support_of of an empty evidence list returned supported, so an approved claim stripped of its evidence stayed authoritative and could be re-approved.

OpenClaw and Hermes are deferred by founder decision D3: Sovereign first owns a minimal channel contract, and the comparison runs only when a concrete conversational channel or agent runtime is needed. Neither may own canonical memory, approvals or credentials, and they are never installed together by default.

Why OpenClaw and Hermes need isolation: OpenClaw runs tools on the host by default and keeps its own sessions, memory and credentials; Hermes keeps MEMORY.md, USER.md and FTS5 session memory. Either would become a shadow personal profile that Sovereign's Forget cannot reach.

Assumptions that remain unverified: that a model runtime on loopback is offline; that the schema 5 migration is safe on large real vaults (only synthetic vaults were tested); that Obsidian opens exports without network requests (no native test has run); that lexical retrieval is good enough for daily use.

Also unverified: whether provenance navigation helps real recall. Benchmark 0003 found 10 of 22 baseline misses discoverable one stored link away, but on a synthetic corpus only, and no lexical method recovered any paraphrase.

The Security Gate is NOT PASSED: no authentication, no application-level encryption, no tested restore on a fresh machine. The six usage thresholds are labels, not permissions; this trial vault is threshold 2, deliberately non-sensitive project use.
Retrieval stays lexical (position R1): Porter stemming recovered 2 more expected items but added 47 irrelevant ones, and BM25 invalidated 51 to 54 of 56 pending previews after one unrelated write.
Builder 0 rule: independent reviewer findings are reviewer-owned; the builder may reproduce, fix or reject a finding with evidence, but only appends responses and never rewrites the finding.
Obsidian is a one-way snapshot export made only on request (decisions D8, D9, D14): no sync, edits are never imported, and forgetting something in Sovereign does not erase exports already made.

claims.text: The first second-brain graph is computed on read because it adds no authority, table or Forget burden
Issue #6 must be repaired before SB-2 holds real data, not before SB-2 development
OpenClaw and Hermes stay deferred until a concrete channel or agent-runtime need exists
The audit narrowed the authority kernel to K1, K2 and a future K3, and split SB-2
Offline loopback inference, large-vault migration safety and Obsidian network silence remain unverified assumptions
